text:
devon: FYI customer ACME reported intermittent 403s on /api/v1/infer from their private deployment and delayed audit-log delivery. Also saw an unexpected billing spike during the window. Escalating to sec + infra @maria @josh

maria: ack. can you paste a short timeline, repro steps, and any control-plane/admin logs you have? curious if this is network-related or an auth/HSM issue.

devon: timeline: 2024-11-08 09:12–09:20 UTC. Repro we ran against their env: 50 rps POSTs to /v1/generate (streaming) from a single host. At ~09:14 we started seeing 403s. Redacted tcpdump snippet below and a control-plane error line.

```
09:14:05.123 IP 10.2.3.4.443 > 10.5.6.7.54022: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 1
09:14:05.124 IP 10.5.6.7.54022 > 10.2.3.4.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:256, ack 512
```

Control-plane extract: `ERR auth: token invalid (status=403) user=svc-acme tenant=acme-tenant-1`
Also customer forwarded a KMS error in their agent: `KMS-ERR 403 wrappingKey not found`

josh: two likely culprits: (1) stateful firewall/NAT conntrack exhaustion or short session timeouts dropping TLS sessions mid-flight, leading to auth failures on rehandshake; (2) KMS/HSM key mismatch or rotation causing envelope decrypt to fail. Do we have conntrack metrics for their region?

ali: i'm on this. customer provided pcap and an audit-sample. they also saw S3 writes for audit events failing around the same time with `403 Forbidden` on the S3 endpoint. I redacted PII and attached minimal snippets.

infra-bot: [alert] nat-gateway-42 conntrack 95% used (2024-11-08T09:15:07Z)

maria: good. short plan:
1) network: check/raise conntrack limits + increase NAT ephemeral port timeout, consider enabling TCP keepalives on the tenant edge.
2) auth: validate customer's KMS key ids in our key-mapping table and confirm HSM key versions; check any recent key rotations.
3) audit delivery: investigate why S3 putObject returned 403 — check IAM role used by audit-forwarder and if the bucket is cross-account or has a deny policy.

josh: quick repro/mitigation commands to try on the edge nodes (LOW-IMPACT):
```
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time=60
# restart audit-forwarder after IAM token refresh
systemctl restart redwood-audit-forwarder
```
I'll prepare a small NAT-rule tweak to bump the conntrack timeout for ephemeral ports and deploy to a canary pool.

devon: additional notes from the customer: audit events between 09:12–09:18 are missing from their console. S3 bucket putObject returned: `403 Forbidden, x-amz-error="AccessDenied"`. Billing: their usage spike was +$1,200 tokens billed between 09:13–09:16.

sam: security questions: is the customer's audit bucket cross-account or in our managed retention bucket? who has kms:Decrypt on the envelope key? if the bucket is cross-account we need to check whether the role used for cross-account writes lost permission during a rotation. also want to confirm retention policy didn't cause accidental deletion + re-ingestion resulting in duplicate billing.

ali: customer confirms cross-account S3 (account B) with a write role in our account (A). I can repro the s3 403 by assuming the role ARN they provided; it fails until the role's trust policy is refreshed. suspect a short-lived credential issue or role update concurrent with their traffic surge.

maria: action items (owners):
- devon: upload full redacted pcap + the three control-plane 403 lines into the incident folder (done/ongoing)
- josh: apply conntrack/timeouts change to canary pool and monitor for 1h; report conntrack utilization and TLS handshake failure rate
- sam: verify KMS/HSM key versions and IAM role permissions for audit S3 writes (check CloudTrail for AssumeRole denies)
- ali: coordinate with customer on exact repro window, confirm role ARN and whether they rotated any keys/roles at that time

Please update thread as you make progress. :eyes:

devon: starting execs now. will post results + logs in ~30m. :thumbsup:
